Vega Automotive Announces Major Expansion in Romania, Boosting Local Industry

Vega Automotive, a leading manufacturer of advanced vehicle components, has unveiled plans for a significant expansion of its Romanian operations, marking a fresh vote of confidence in the country’s automotive sector. The company will invest €120 million to extend its existing facility in the industrial zone near Craiova, with the aim of increasing production capacity and introducing new product lines focused on electric and hybrid vehicle technologies.

The expansion, set to be completed in phases by 2026, is expected to create 450 new jobs, ranging from engineering roles to skilled technicians and support staff. Vega Automotive’s Romanian subsidiary currently employs 900 people and supplies major automakers across Europe. The new investment will see the site’s footprint nearly double, with the addition of state-of-the-art assembly lines and a research and development center dedicated to next-generation powertrains.

“We see enormous potential in Romania as a hub for our advanced manufacturing and innovation activities,” said Markus Klein, Chief Operating Officer of Vega Automotive, at a press conference in Bucharest on Thursday. “The local workforce is highly skilled, and the government’s commitment to infrastructure and education gives us confidence in the long-term prospects here.”

The move comes amid growing interest in Romania’s automotive sector, which accounted for 13% of the country’s GDP in 2023, according to the Romanian Automotive Manufacturers Association. The region’s strategic location, competitive labor costs, and improving logistics have made it an increasingly attractive destination for foreign direct investment.

Local officials welcomed the announcement. “This expansion underlines our region’s strengths as a center for industrial growth and technological development,” said Craiova Mayor Elena Dumitru. She highlighted the city’s technical university and vocational training programs, which have played a key role in supplying qualified personnel to the sector.

Industry analysts say the investment could have a ripple effect, strengthening Romania’s position in the European automotive supply chain. “When global players like Vega Automotive commit to expanding here, it sends a positive signal to other investors and boosts confidence in the sector’s stability,” commented Andrei Ionescu, an automotive industry consultant based in Bucharest.

The project is backed by a package of incentives from the Romanian government, including tax breaks and support for workforce training, as part of a broader initiative to accelerate the transition to electric mobility.

Construction work is scheduled to begin later this year, with the first phase of the expanded facility expected to become operational by mid-2025. Vega Automotive’s expansion is poised to further cement Romania’s reputation as a rising force in Europe’s evolving automotive landscape.
